What's attached in this email (zip of the key artifacts):

- egress-proofing-checklist.xlsx — itemized checklist you can use in your audit (deny-by-default settings, proxy placement options, and recommended firewall rules).

Quick notes/high level:
- Control plane is intentionally separated: control-plane agents communicate to a management endpoint over mTLS on TCP 443 from a restricted management network. Data-plane inference traffic never traverses the control plane (we use signed session tokens and per-tenant routing).
- Egress: typical deployments require outbound to Redwood-managed telemetry sinks and optional image/model repositories. We support proxying and allowlisting; the checklist includes an opt-in zero-egress mode if Acme wishes to host model artifacts locally.
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key). Integration notes are in the second-round docs (we'll attach technical notes in follow-up).
- Runbook: I've included the provisioning checklist rows in the spreadsheet; we'll extract a more narrative runbook section for your ops team if needed.

Timeline: we can deliver a runbook excerpt and KMS integration notes by EOD tomorrow (2026-06-08). Does that align with the Wednesday review?

Jordan / Vanessa — adding a few technical clarifications that we frequently get asked in audits, and attaching the raw notes: wg-egress-patterns.txt and kms-integration-notes.md.

Key technical points (short):
- Control plane endpoints: outbound-only from management nodes to control.redwood-inference.com (mTLS mutual auth). Source IPs are pinned per-customer in Dedicated/Private. You can enforce egress at the subnet-level; our agents will still function if only 443 outbound is allowed to the pinned endpoints.
- Data plane: inference traffic (client -> tenant gateway -> local runtime) is kept inside your VPC. Only metadata/telemetry and model fetches (if using Redwood model registry) leave the tenancy boundary — both are optional.
- Egress-proofing options:
  * Option A (Default): allowlist minimal endpoints and enforce proxying for model pulls and telemetry.
  * Option B (Zero-egress): host models in your registry and disable telemetry; this requires local model-store mounting or airgapped model sync via signed bundles.
- KMS integration: we support two modes: 1) Redwood-managed encryption keys (recommended for fast onboarding) and 2) Customer-managed KMS via our KMS plugin. When 2 is selected, keys never leave your KMS; we store only key references and perform envelope encryption at the runtime. Key rotation: supported via automated rewrap with staged rollout (notes in kms-integration-notes.md).

Audit logs:
- We can provide JSON-line samples of operational events (token issuance, tenant deploy, model fetch) and a mapping doc for SIEM ingestion. If you have an event-schema example, send it; otherwise we will include our default sample.

Attachments (stubs): wg-egress-patterns.txt, kms-integration-notes.md

I can follow up with a short network-savvy one-pager for your reviewers if helpful.

—Kim
Kimberly Park
Network & Deployability Engineering — Redwood
